A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReCreate and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, action-distribution analyses, temperature sensitivity, and optimization costs.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds update-iteration, model-generalization, development-set sensitivity, and significance analyses.

M1.justification: The experience retrieval mechanism, creation router, hierarchical instance-to-domain updates, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The optimizer prompts and implementation appendix are also retained apart from editorial corrections.

E1.justification: Appendix J adds development examples from SWE-bench Full excluding Verified, extending the development-data source beyond v1's sampled Verified examples. The original four domains, thirteen main evaluation subsets, and SWE-bench Lite analysis remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CoT, SBA, Self-Refine, LIVE, OPRO, ExpeL, ADAS, and AgentSquare. The change from ORPO to OPRO in its header corrects the name already given in v1's prose. Added model comparisons and significance tests use existing comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds several supplementary protocols: twenty single-case development sets with four update iterations and test-case pass rates; Claude Opus 4.5 as both optimizer and task agent; Gemini-2.5-Flash and GPT-4o-mini task agents; and development sets of 20, 50, or 100 cases. The original main experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 and Appendices H and J add substantial analyses of recovery across updates, dependence on model choice, and sensitivity to development-set size and composition. The original component ablations and temperature analysis remain. The Django case study is retained from v1's Appendix J, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix I newly reports exact McNemar tests against SBA, ExpeL, and AgentSquare, with a stated sample size of 1,681 and significance threshold of 0.05. Appendix J also reports three sampled development-set compositions and standard deviation 0.28. These statistical assessments were absent from v1; they do not establish repeated runs of the original main experiment.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4 and the cost results retain their numerical values. New Figures 7, 10, and 11 and Tables 5–7 add substantial results, including reported average gains of 8.3 and 8.7 points for Gemini-2.5-Flash and GPT-4o-mini, and scores of 57.4, 60.4, and 60.8 for development sizes 20, 50, and 100. These are additional settings, not improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: The scaffold decomposition, task and trajectory definitions, bi-level objective, and experience-based update formulation remain mathematically unchanged. v2 introduces no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim experience-driven domain-agent creation through the same three components and consistent advantages over human-designed and automated-generation baselines. Replacing some occurrences of domain agents with specialized agents does not materially alter these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that scaffold improvements capture largely model-agnostic patterns, that additional development experience improves performance, and that performance is stable across sampled development sets. The infrastructure and frozen-model limitations are condensed without materially changing their meaning.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly clarifies DA-Code's continuous scores and the other benchmarks' binary outcomes. Added experiments document model choices, iteration limits, and development-data sampling exclusions. The implementation appendix, substantive prompt contents, and code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds GUI-related citations and expands Appendix B's context-optimization and memory-evolution references, including replacing the Richelieu example with newer citations and discussion. The central positioning against metric-driven agent generation and existing self-evolution methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes distributed grammatical and terminology corrections, updates affiliations, adds acknowledgements and analysis headings, and shortens the limitations section. Appendices E and F exchange order, with later appendices renumbered. Most existing exposition and narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the empirical displays through a front-page summary chart, update-iteration plots, model-comparison plots, and three statistical/sensitivity tables. Existing figures are relocated and renumbered, and Tables 1 and 2 gain revised formatting and highlighting. The summary chart redisplays existing results; the architecture and appendix case illustrations are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The matched-model control and added backbone and development-set studies strengthen empirical support for the retained method. Metric clarification and editing also improve reporting. However, Appendix I's significance scope is unclear: it claims thirteen datasets, while N=1681 matches the documented binary-outcome datasets after excluding continuous-score DA-Code. The additions provide a supported but limited net quality improvement.
